CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Sample ID: [redacted ID]
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Hospital/Clinic: [redacted location]

SAMPLE INFORMATION
Sample Type: Fetal tissue
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal genetic testing

TESTS PERFORMED
1. Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
2. Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY

Array CGH:
- Platform: GenArray 3000 oligonucleotide array
- Probe density: ~60,000 genome-wide probes
- Median resolution: 120kb
- Analysis software: GenScan Pro
- Reference genome: GRCh37/hg19
- DNA extracted from fetal tissue and hybridized against reference DNA
- Log2 ratios calculated and analyzed for copy number variations

QF-PCR:
- Multiplex QF-PCR analysis for rapid aneuploidy detection
- Markers analyzed for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y
- Assessment for triploidy included

RESULTS

Array CGH Result:
arr(1-22,X,Y)x2

No copy number imbalances detected across all autosomes (chromosomes 1-22) and sex chromosomes (X,Y). Results are consistent with a normal male chromosome complement.

QF-PCR Result:
Normal male pattern confirmed
No evidence of trisomy 13, 18, or 21
No evidence of triploidy
Sex chromosome complement: XY

INTERPRETATION
The array CGH analysis shows no genomic imbalances of known clinical significance. No deletions or duplications of pathogenic significance were identified. The resolution of this test is approximately 120kb; therefore, smaller imbalances below this threshold would not be detected.

The QF-PCR results support the array findings, confirming a normal male karyotype with no evidence of common aneuploidies or triploidy.

LIMITATIONS
- Array CGH cannot detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements (translocations, inversions)
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be reliably detected
- Single gene mutations and methylation abnormalities are not detected by this method
- Uniparental disomy cannot be excluded

CONCLUSION
No abnormality detected. Chromosome complement normal (male).

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis required on this sample.

This result should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings and other diagnostic tests.

Authorized by: Dr. [redacted name]
Consultant Clinical Scientist
Date: [redacted date]
